result.summary:
I found no critical or high defect in the EV, fee or price math with the default configuration (live only, score trigger, WORST_CASE devig). Every order the app sends has EV at or above its minimum after Novig's fee at every price it can fill, measured against Pinnacle's fair as read at decision time. I checked this by reading the code line by line, by Python ports of Devig.kt (4 methods) and of judge/positiveDepth/size/priceText, and by property tests: 167,685 random ladders gave 0 EV-at-limit violations, 0 off-grid limits, 0 price-string mismatches and 0 stake overruns; 55,529 two-way and 7,273 three-way Pinnacle lines gave 0 cases where WORST_CASE exceeded any method. Novig's catalog charges 0.06, not 0.03, on MLB, NHL and NCAAF game lines, and the app reads each market's own fee object, so that is handled.

The weaknesses are all about what is judged, not how: the fee flag in pregame mode, no sanity ceiling on a too-good EV (the STANDING trigger can bet them), no check of real fills against the fair, and a few settings and accounting corners. Two things to know before tonight:
1. Pregame mode (opt-in) can judge a just-kicked-off game as fee-free for up to about 40 s. At 0.06 coefficients this can flip a 3% EV bet negative.
2. The STANDING trigger (opt-in) is unsafe. On the tape, 162 of 285 qualifying rows showed EV of 25% or more against a Pinnacle price that had sat unchanged for a median 155 s. The confirm dialog also describes a Pinnacle move requirement that STANDING does not have.

Separately, my re-run of the replay with exact fees and WORST_CASE gives only n=16 at the default rule: +10.0% EV at decision, +3.3% against Pinnacle's fair 30 s later and +6.7% 120 s later. At the loosest score-driven setting (n=26) the edge against Pinnacle 120 s later is -0.7%. That sample is too small to call the edge proven.

findings.title: Pregame mode judges a just-kicked-off game as fee-free (fee flag comes from a catalog up to ~40 s old)
findings.scenario: Only with 'Also pregame moves' on. evaluate() sets live = t.event.status != OPEN_PREGAME, and t.event is the NovigEvent from the last catalog fetch (DISCOVER_MS = 30 s, plus the CloudFront cache). Pairs are rebuilt only on a new catalog (catalogDirty) or an event-count change, and eligibleNow() checks e.startMs > now only inside rematch. For up to about 30-40 s after kickoff, a pre-game pair keeps being judged with live = false, so EvMath.quote adds no fee. Novig decides liveness at match time (docs.novig.com/api/concepts/fees: 'We decide whether an event is live at match time'), so the IOC fill is charged. Example on an MLB/NHL/NCAAF market (coefficient 0.06): fair 0.26, ask 0.252, min EV 3%. The app computes 0.26/0.252 - 1 = +3.17% and bets. The real cost is 0.252 + 0.06*0.252*0.748 = 0.2633, so the real EV is -1.26%. At coefficient 0.03 and p about 0.5 the fee is 1.5% of cost; at 0.06 and p about 0.25 it is about 4.5%, larger than any EV chip (2-5%). The same stale pair can also be judged against a Pinnacle prematch line that stops updating at kickoff, but I could not confirm that on tape: neither tape contains a prematch-to-live transition.
findings.evidence: Code: PinnLiveRunner.kt:314 (live flag), :177 (PREGAME only in the catalog when pregame is on), :248 (rematch cadence), :295-296 (eligibleNow), :406 (DISCOVER_MS = 30_000). Docs fetched from docs.novig.com/fees.md and /api/concepts/fees.md: liveness 'evaluated at match time, not when the order was placed'. Live public catalog (2026-10-08): MLB 71/71, NHL 164/164 and NCAAF 300/300 sampled game-line markets carry coefficient 0.06 WHEN_LIVE. Numbers computed in Python (scratchpad/audit_math/t6_wc_tables.py). With pregame off, the catalog holds only LIVE/DELAYED events, so live is always true and the default mode is unaffected.
findings.fix: In evaluate(), compute novigLive = t.event.status != STATUS_PREGAME || pe.live || now >= t.event.startsTs - 120_000. Skip pregame targets (return before judge) once now >= startsTs - 60_000, because GOLIVE voids the book and the price is not comparable. Also re-run rematch() when the clock crosses a matched game's start time rather than waiting for the next catalog.

findings.title: No ceiling on EV or price gap, and the STANDING trigger has no freshness test, so stale Pinnacle prices look like huge edges and are bet
findings.scenario: STANDING only requires the Pinnacle price to be unchanged for 30 s and open; nothing bounds how old it may be. judge() also has no upper bound on EV, so any matching or orientation error, or a frozen Pinnacle line, shows up as an enormous 'edge' and goes straight to an order. Example from the pooled tape: WNBA total, Pinnacle fair 0.49 for a price unchanged for 122 s, Novig ask 0.165, depth 20,000 -> EV +190%; NBA moneyline fair 0.355 vs ask 0.003 -> EV +11,400%. With stake $2 the trader would send IOC orders for these. A bet whose EV is 100%+ is almost certainly a stale line, a finished game or a mapped-to-wrong-outcome error, not an edge. The confirm dialog (PinnText.confirm) also says each bet needs 'a Pinnacle move of at least X', which is false for STANDING.
findings.evidence: Tape replay with the app's exact rule (Python port, WORST_CASE devig, per-market fee, scratchpad/audit_math/t3_replay_ev.py): STANDING-qualified rows (price stable >=30 s, EV >=5%, fair 0.08-0.92, depth >=20) = 285 rows over 30 markets; EV >=25%: 162 rows/17 markets, median Pinnacle price age 155 s; EV >=50%: 71 rows/10 markets; EV >=100%: 18 rows/5 markets; EV >=500%: 5 rows, one market, price age 1,013 s. Under SCORE/MOVE triggers (t4_trigger_replay.py) only 2 of 55 triggers exceeded 20% EV, and both were -22%/-35% against Pinnacle's later fair (n=2, so weak evidence). RESEARCH.md 116.2 itself notes the +100% 'standing' rows are stale prices. Code: LiveEdge.kt:112, :114-123; the PinnLine has no last-confirmed timestamp (PinnBook.kt:225 returns early for unchanged re-sends).
findings.fix: (1) Add LiveRules.maxEv (e.g. 0.30) and LiveSkip.TOO_GOOD in judge(): if (quote.evPercent > rules.maxEv) return Skip, journalled and counted, since a real lag rarely exceeds 30% after a 5%-chip filter. (2) Add PinnLine.lastSeenAtMs, set on every accepted frame including unchanged re-sends, and for STANDING require now - lastSeenAtMs <= 10_000 and stable <= 120_000. (3) Make PinnText.confirm() name the trigger and pregame setting instead of always saying a Pinnacle move is required.

findings.title: Real fills are never compared with the fair: a wrong fee model or price would run all night unnoticed
findings.scenario: After fills come back, trade() records paid/fee and logs the Tracker bet, but nothing checks that the real cost per contract, (paid+fee)/(filled*0.01), still clears the fair the bet was judged on. In-play fee behaviour on a real order has never been verified (NOVIG_API.md 21: 'The first real in-play order is the test'). If the live fee were charged differently from c*P*(1-P) per $1 payout, the catalog coefficient were stale, or the event were charged when judged free (finding 1), every fill would be worse than judged and only the settled-loss halt (days later) would notice.
findings.evidence: Code: PinnLiveTrader.kt:312-330 (no realized-EV test); BetTracker.logApi computes evPercentAtBet = fair/cost - 1 (BetTracker.kt:526) but nothing acts on it. Judge-side math is sound by property test, so this is a safety net for the unverified fee/ordering assumptions, not a found defect.
findings.fix: After computing paid/fee/filled: val realCost = (paid + fee) / (filled * 0.01); val realEv = c.verdict.fair / realCost - 1; if (realEv < 0.0) haltNow("first fill costs more than judged (EV %.1f%%): check Novig's fee"). Also compare fee with c.fee.coefficient*avgPrice*(1-avgPrice)*filled*0.01 and halt if the actual fee differs by more than 1e-4 dollars per fill. This turns the first real in-play fill into the fee check.

findings.title: Fills list is trusted even when shorter than the order's own filled quantity (only the empty case is retried)
findings.scenario: settle() re-reads fills once (after 600 ms) only when fills.isEmpty() and the order is FILLED. An IOC that sweeps k resting orders prints k fill rows (NOVIG_API.md 18: 'a taker order that sweeps several resting orders prints one row per resting order'). If the first read returns only some rows, trade() takes filled = sum of those rows, so paid/feePaid and the Tracker bet understate what Novig actually filled. BetTracker.logApi de-duplicates by orderId, so the missing fills are never merged by a later call. The per-game and per-day caps in size() then see less spend than was really spent, and 'spent' in the status is low. EV and price judgement are unaffected. I could not show fill-row lag in the data; the existing empty-list retry suggests it was seen or expected.
findings.evidence: Code: PinnLiveTrader.kt:312, :319-322, :333-349; NovigOrder has qty/remaining/status (NovigTradingClient.kt:14-33) but they are not used to check the fills total; BetTracker.kt:551-556 returns the existing bet for a repeated orderId.
findings.fix: In settle(): if o.status == "FILLED" and fills.sumOf { it.qty } < o.qty, re-read (2-3 times, 300 ms apart). If still short, record UNCONFIRMED and haltNow('fills do not add up to the order'). For CANCELED partials, apply the same test with the filled quantity the order reports once the field is verified.

findings.title: MIN_STAKE floor of $1 overrides a per-bet limit below $1
findings.scenario: VigilantApp.pinnTradeRules() sets stake = min(pinnLiveStake, apiMaxStake). The apiMaxStake field accepts any amount from $0.01 (TypedNumber.kt:66). size() then applies r.stake.coerceIn(MIN_STAKE = 1.0, MAX_STAKE = 25.0). With apiMaxStake = $0.50 and pinnLiveStake = $2, the rule stake is $0.50 but the order is sized for $1.00, twice the limit Tj typed. The wallet gate (pinnGate) checks the unfloored $0.50*1.2. The exposure is bounded (under $1 per bet over the limit, and the per-game and per-day caps still apply), so this is low.
findings.evidence: Code: VigilantApp.kt:1050 (min with apiMaxStake), PinnLiveTrader.kt:264 (coerceIn), :32-33 (constants), ApiBettingUi.kt:296 (typed field), TypedNumber.kt:66 (min 0.01).
findings.fix: Do not raise the stake: val stake = minOf(r.stake, LiveTradeLimits.MAX_STAKE); if (stake < LiveTradeLimits.MIN_STAKE) return null (skip as 'limit reached').

findings.title: POWER and MULTIPLICATIVE devig chips are not conservative; the safe default can be switched off in one tap
findings.scenario: WORST_CASE is the per-side minimum of four methods and is therefore never kinder than any of them (verified). The chips offer POWER and MULTIPLICATIVE, which are the kind ones on one side each. Dog side, Pinnacle +400/-600 (overround 5.7%), Novig ask 0.175, in-play coefficient 0.03: MULTIPLICATIVE fair 0.1892 gives EV +5.5% (passes a 5% chip); WORST_CASE/POWER fair 0.1607 gives -10.4%. Favourite side, -600/+440, ask 0.80: POWER fair 0.8439 gives EV +4.9%; WORST_CASE/MULTIPLICATIVE fair 0.8223 gives +2.2%. The confirm dialog does not name the devig method.
findings.evidence: Python port of Devig.kt (scratchpad/audit_math/devig.py, t6_wc_tables.py). Over -1500..+1500 lines with overround up to 9%, the minimum is MULTIPLICATIVE for the negative-price side in 99% of lines and POWER for the positive-price side. For 2-way lines Shin equals additive, so the four methods act as three. Settings default is WORST_CASE (ScanSettings.kt:385).
findings.fix: Remove the POWER and MULTIPLICATIVE chips from the live section, or add a line under them ('less conservative: can show +EV where worst-case shows -10%') and include the method name in the real-bets confirmation text.

findings.title: Replay that justified the defaults charges 0.03 on every market; 53 of 160 tape markets (MLB, NHL, NCAAF) carry 0.06
findings.scenario: The study tool hard-codes FEE_C = 0.03 (lines 16 and 350-351). NOVIG_API.md section 8 and the MarketFee.GAME comment say all game lines are 0.03. The live catalog and the tape say otherwise: MLB, NHL and NCAAF game lines are 0.06 WHEN_LIVE (NBA, NFL, WNBA and the soccer leagues are 0.03). The Pinnodds order path is not affected, because it reads t.market.fee per market (PinnLiveRunner.kt:308), but the published edge numbers (RESEARCH.md 116.2) overstate those leagues, and fee-less fallbacks in other features (BurstTrader.kt:342, BetTracker.kt:350/425/895, CnoBooks.kt:241) use MarketFee.GAME.
findings.evidence: Pooled tape: 107 markets at 0.03 (NBA, WNBA) and 53 at 0.06 (MLB 11, NCAAF 23, NHL 19). Live public catalog today: MLB 71/71, NHL 164/164 and NCAAF 300/300 sampled markets at 0.06, NBA 300, NFL 300 and soccer leagues at 0.03. Re-running the qualifying rows with true fees: in 0.06 markets EV was overstated by 2.64 points on average (124 rows), and 9 rows fall under 5%.
findings.fix: Have the study tool read fee.coefficient from each 'mkt' record. Update NOVIG_API.md section 8 and the MarketFee.GAME comment ('read per market; MLB/NHL/NCAAF game lines are 0.06'). In BurstTrader's fill-less fallback use the market's own fee.

findings.title: Comparisons are NaN-permissive (a NaN fair, ask or coefficient passes every check)
findings.scenario: judge() skips with 'if (x < min)' style tests (fair band, move, EV). Every comparison against NaN is false, so a NaN would pass them all and produce a Bet with NaN EV. I found no real path to NaN: the devig outputs are finite, and Pinnacle prices outside (-100, 100) are dropped. A fee coefficient such as "NaN" would parse, because Kotlin's toDoubleOrNull accepts it. This is defence in depth only.
findings.evidence: LiveEdge.kt:104, 108, 117; NovigPublicClient.kt FeeDto.toDomain() (coefficient?.toDoubleOrNull()). 46,003 Pinnacle market updates in the tapes produced no out-of-range or crossed prices, so there is no empirical NaN risk.
findings.fix: Write the EV test as if (!(quote.evPercent >= rules.minEv)) return Skip(EV) and the fair band as if (!(fair in minFair..maxFair)); require coefficient.isFinite() when parsing the fee.

findings.title: EV is judged once at decision; nothing re-checks Pinnacle's price just before the order goes out
findings.scenario: The IOC limit protects against Novig moving (a worse level is never filled). Nothing protects against Pinnacle moving between judge() and Novig's match. After the decision, attempt() runs gate(), the loss lookup (tracker.all() reads the store), size(), then a REST round trip of about 120 ms. If Pinnacle re-prices against the side in that time (common right after a score), the order still goes at the old fair, whose settle test (500 ms unchanged) was only applied at decision.
findings.evidence: Code: PinnLiveTrader.kt:221-248 (no re-judge), :290-291 (place). Nothing in the trader records decision-to-send time (decisionMs measures Pinnacle change to decision; sendToEndMs measures send to end).
findings.fix: Pass the trader a cheap staleness callback: just before place(), refuse if the line's changedAtMs differs from c.pinnChangedAtMs (a volatile read of PinnLine.changedAtMs), or post a recheck message to the runner's consumer and send only on a still-valid verdict.

checked_ok: EvMath.quote/positiveDepth: cost = price + c*p*(1-p) is strictly increasing in price for c <= 0.5 (checked all 999 prices). EV% is therefore monotone, positiveDepth's break at the first failing level is exact, and the EV at limitPrice (the worst passing level, fee included) is the lowest EV of any fill the IOC can make. Property test over 167,685 random Novig ladders, coefficients 0/0.03/0.06, live and not live, min EV 2-5%: 0 violations.

Fees.takerFee = coefficient*p*(1-p) per $1 payout, with a contract paying 1 cent. Matches docs.novig.com (Fee = c*P*(1-P)*N*1 cent, P the fill price; examples 10,000@0.50 = $0.75, 100@0.50 = $0.0075; half-up to 5 decimals; no cent floor). The older page's 'qty/100' warning is the same convention. The ledger quantization (5 decimal places) is negligible.

Fee schedule is read per market (NovigPublicClient FeeDto, judge/size use t.market.fee). Unreadable or unknown 'charged' means fee == null, so the market is skipped ('market has no fee data'), never assumed free. MLB/NHL/NCAAF at 0.06 are handled.

WHEN_LIVE vs ALWAYS vs DELAYED: Fees.isCharged is right. In live-only mode the catalog holds only OPEN_INGAME/DELAYED events, so live is always true. DELAYED is treated as charged, which is conservative (Novig does not charge fills during a suspension). Sizing always assumes the fee (size() passes true), also conservative. The only fee-flag hole is pregame mode (finding 1).

Price grid: the 279-step grid is closed under x -> 1000-x (all grid m, checked), so 1 - bid is always on the grid. In the tape all 9,486 best bids were on the grid and none of 4,663 two-sided reads crossed. limitPrice is always one of the take levels and so on the grid. BigDecimal.valueOf(price).setScale(3, HALF_UP) renders every grid ask exactly (checked for all 279 values).

Order sizing units: perContract = (limit + fee(limit)) * 0.01 and qty = floor(stake/perContract) never exceeds the stake (0 overruns in 167k trials), and is capped by the depth at EV >= min and by the game/day remainder. Fee at the worst price is the highest cost per contract, so the stake cap is conservative. An IOC with qty <= depth cannot fill at a price whose EV is under the minimum; partial fills are at the same or better levels.

Tracker record: logApi computes price = paid/payout, cost = (paid+fee)/payout and evPercentAtBet = fair/cost - 1 from the real fills, the same definition as EvQuote.evPercent. NovigFill.cost excludes the fee (docs), so paid + feePaid in the caps is not double-counted; an absent fee field (uncharged fill) correctly reads as 0.

Devig WORST_CASE: Python port of Devig.kt (same bounds, tolerance, step caps). Over 55,529 two-way lines (-1500..+1500 both sides, overround <= 12%) and 7,273 random three-way lines, 0 cases where the per-side minimum exceeds any method; power and Shin sum to 1 within 4e-14. It never overstates a side relative to the four methods. It does not sum to 1 (tape median 0.994, min 0.915; -1500/+800 gives 0.968), which lowers both sides' fair and is conservative. Residual assumption: if a book loads its margin onto the side being bought, the truth can sit below all four methods, by up to (overround - what WC removes), about 1.8-2.4 points at 5% overround and about 4.5 points at the 9% maxOverround limit. This is a modelling limit, not a bug.
Both sides of one market cannot both pass: the sum of asks is >= 1 on an uncrossed book while the WORST_CASE fairs sum to < 1, so the app cannot buy both outcomes of a market as two 'edges'.

A stale or wrong Novig book cannot produce a worse fill: the IOC limit is the judged worst level, a book with a sequence gap is dropped (StreamBooks.book returns null), and a missing book is skipped. NovigStream.live() stamps fetchedAtMs = now, but that only affects reporting.

Devig failures: PinnBook drops an update whose prices are crossed (sum < 1) or inside (-100, 100), leaving the old line. The tapes show this never happens: 46,003 open moneyline/spread/total updates, 0 crossed or out-of-range.

Soccer: Novig lists only x.5 spread/total strikes (EPL, MLS, La Liga, Serie A, Bundesliga, Ligue 1, Champions League checked), so Pinnacle's quarter-ball lines (e.g. -0.25) never match and cannot be mispriced as binary events; three-way Pinnacle moneylines are excluded in LiveTarget.line (DRAW) and by outcomes.size != 2.

Spread/total orientation arithmetic (side(), swapped, strike sign) checked by hand for all four home/away x swapped combinations: the outcome bought is the one whose fair is used. No duplicate non-alternate period-0 moneyline lines per event in the tapes (0 of 1,033 events).

Order body: price string, qty as a number, tif IOC, clientId UUID. Fills are read by order id; an unfilled IOC is MISSED, never assumed filled; an order that is not terminal within 2.5 s halts the trader.
